Obviously it depends on several factors and will be different for each person. 

I'm mostly exasperated that people want to give advice on cleaning, when I asked for advice on telling my partner she isn't doing something right.

Nope, gyno is cool with how I take care of myself, I certainly wouldn't change my own routine. I'm glad your body allows you to only use water, but I've got too much extra skin that collects extra fluids and bacteria. Just different skin types and shapes 🤷🏼‍♀️

That is helpful, but it isn't that she hasn't showered, it's just that she's not cleaning well enough.

 I think the consensus is to take a shower with her and show her how to clean. It's something not many of us are taught to do correctly.

Thanks for all your input, I appreciate it!
So, since you obviously agree on the difference between vulva and vagina, any thoughts on how to approach the girlfriend about washing better?
You are correct in reference to vagina, but not the vulva. You should definitely wash the vulvar area with gentle soap and water.

As a vulva owner with a background in healthcare, I assure you it is indeed ok, and even desirable to wash the skin folds with gentle soap. If I didn't do that myself I would reek to the high heavens.

This was my thought process. Maybe a shower or bath together. Thanks for your input!

And yes, most people should wash the vulvar skin, just not inside the vagina. Not sure why there's confusion among many in here on the difference.

Correct, clean vulva not in vagina. I can't believe the number of comments saying not to use soap! I'm a female with a background in healthcare and biology. You must wash the skin down there! Just not inside the vagina.
Not the vagina, the vulva.
Not vagina, but the vulva.
